Comment: Grants and removes AppStream application assignments to match active TEAM sessions. Decisions come from TEAM's own executions, never from the requests table status.

Event: request id.Comment: Pipe input is a batch of stream records. A manual test can pass {"requestId": "..."} instead.

Event: Schedule run.Comment: TEAM names the Schedule run after the request id, and only starts it after approval.

Event: Grant run.Comment: userId, username and accountId come from the Grant run input, which only TEAM's backend sets.

Sweep: in-progress requests.Comment: Candidates only. Every one is verified against TEAM's executions before it counts.

Sweep: targets.Comment: One target per managed ledger row, so every tracked principal is re-checked. Requests not already tracked by a ledger row get their own targets, grouped by username and application but limited to those untracked ids, so a reused username cannot hide a new principal behind an old one. Each target carries its candidate request ids from the sweep's query.

R: isolated.Comment: One target's failure is recorded and the others carry on.

R: candidates.Comment: This user's in-progress requests, every page. The status is only a hint; each is verified next.

R: verify.Comment: Only TEAM-style UUID request ids are checked. Anything else could make the execution ARN invalid, so it is ignored rather than allowed to fail the run.

V: Schedule run.Comment: No Schedule run means TEAM never approved this request.

V: Grant matches?.Comment: Positive match only, so a missing field fails closed. The IdC user id decides once known: usernames can be renamed or reused.

V: Grant position.Comment: Active means the Grant run is in its session Wait. A failed grant never reaches it.

V: waiting?.Comment: TEAM writes 'in progress' a moment before the Wait starts, so retry briefly.

V: early revoke?.Comment: An early revoke starts a Revoke run named after the request id while the Grant run keeps waiting.

V: account access.Comment: The account assignment TEAM created for this session must still exist. TEAM deletes the shared assignment when one of two overlapping sessions on the same account and permission set ends, so the other has lost access too. A deleted permission set or account means no access either.

V: access?.Comment: Every page is read. A new assignment can take a few seconds to provision, so look again briefly before deciding it has gone.

R: principal known?.Comment: No principal: nothing of ours to manage. A newly discovered one goes round once more, ledger first.

R: decide.Comment: An assignment that already existed and is not owned by us is recorded as preexisting and never removed.

R: settle?.Comment: The triggering session ended but others are still active. TEAM's delete of a shared account assignment may not have finished, so look once more before keeping access.

R: settle.Comment: Once per target, tracked apart from the pass count so a lost lock cannot use it up.

R: claim.Comment: Ownership is recorded before the create, so a failure after it can never leave an assignment we created looking preexisting.

R: release.Comment: Released only after the delete, so a failed delete stays owned and is retried. If another run claimed it meanwhile, the lock fails and the next pass recreates the assignment.

Arguments.UpdateExpression: REMOVE activeRequestIds, managed SET updatedAt = :t, rev = :next

R: again?.Comment: Verify everything again after a create, a delete, a conflict or a lost lock.

R: principal known for hint?.Comment: With a known principal, read the ledger first: its ids are re-verified too, so an edited status cannot drop a live session.

R: confirm owned.Comment: Unconditional: this run created the assignment, so it must stay owned even if another run released the row meanwhile. The re-check then removes it if no session is active.

R: ledger.Comment: Read before verifying, consistently, so every conditional write below is against what this pass saw.

R: track delete.Comment: A delete needs two consecutive passes that both decide delete.

R: confirm wait.Comment: Never remove access on a single look: wait, then verify everything again.

R: lock for delete.Comment: If any run wrote the row since this pass read it (for example a new session), the lock fails and nothing is deleted.

R: query?.Comment: The sweep's first pass reuses its own query. Every later pass, and every event, queries afresh. With no username to query by, only the ledger and trigger ids are checked.

Any target failed?.Comment: Every target has been tried. Fail the run if any errored, so the failed-runs alarm fires.
